lede: The revelation had paused. Then he saw the angel again, filling the horizon, and went home trembling and asking to be covered. The words that came next ended the quiet years for good: stand up, and warn.

names.name: al-Muddaththir
names.note: After the way it addresses the Prophet ﷺ: you who are covered in your cloak — the dithār, the outer wrap he had asked his family to put over him.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all. Ibn al-Jawzī notes only that Muqātil held one ayah of it, the long thirty-first, to be Madinan. Its opening is among the earliest of all revelation: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh held that it was the very first, and the majority, as Ibn Kathīr records, that the first was the opening of al-ʿAlaq and that this came first after the pause.
revelation.when: The start of the mission: the first revelation after the pause that followed Ḥirāʾ

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ المُدَّثِّرِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِإجْماعِهِمْ وَقالَ مُقاتِلٌ: فِيها مِنَ المَدَنِيِّ آيَةٌ
عَنْ جَابِرٍ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ: أَوَّلُ شَيْءٍ نَزَلَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾ وَخَالَفَهُ الْجُمْهُورُ فَذَهَبُوا إِلَى أَنَّ أَوَّلَ الْقُرْآنِ نُزُولًا

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والنَّحّاسُ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ المُدَّثِّرِ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Naḥḥās and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: After the first words in the cave of Ḥirāʾ, the revelation stopped for a time. The Prophet ﷺ described its return himself, as Jābir relates. “While I was walking I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Ḥirāʾ, seated on a throne between the sky and the earth. I was struck with awe of him, and went back and said: cover me, cover me.” And Allah sent down: “O you enveloped in your cloak — arise and warn; magnify your Lord; purify your garments; and shun all defilement.” After that, he said, the revelation came strongly and in close succession.
Those first seven ayat are a commission in the fewest possible words: the task, and the character of the one who is to carry it out.

The middle of the surah belongs to a later moment and a particular man. Quraysh needed something to tell the pilgrims who would soon arrive and hear the Qurʾan. They went to al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, the richest and most respected of them, who had himself been shaken by what he heard. The surah describes him at work: he reflected, and he plotted; he looked; he frowned and scowled; he turned away in pride — and said, “This is nothing but magic handed down. This is nothing but the word of a human being.” The reply names where he is going: Saqar. “Over it are nineteen.”

The number was meant as a test, and it worked as one. Abū Jahl is reported to have mocked it: nineteen — surely ten of you can deal with each of them.{reported} The long ayah that follows says exactly this: We have made their number a trial for those who disbelieve, a certainty for those given the Book, and an increase in faith for those who believe.

occasions.title: After the pause
occasions.text: “I stayed in retreat at Ḥirāʾ for a month. When my retreat was over I came down into the bottom of the valley, and I was called. I looked in front of me and behind me, to my right and to my left, and saw no one. Then I raised my head, and there he was, upon a throne in the air…” He went to Khadījah and said, “Cover me,” and these ayat were sent down.
occasions.source: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh: al-Bukhārī (4922–4926) and Muslim (161).

evidence.quote: فَرَوى البُخارِيُّ ومُسْلِمٌ في "صَحِيحِيهِما" مِن حَدِيثِ جابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قالَ: حَدَّثَنا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ قالَ: «جاوَرْتُ بِحِراءَ شَهْرًا، فَلَمّا قَضَيْتُ جِوارِي نَزَلْتُ فاسْتَبْطَنْتُ بَطْنَ الوادِي، فَنُودِيتُ

occasions.title: Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah
occasions.text: The commentators relate that these ayat came down about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, whom Quraysh consulted on what to say of the Qurʾan. He admitted that it was not poetry and not the muttering of a soothsayer, and then settled on calling it magic that parts a man from his family.
occasions.source: Ibn Kathīr and Ibn al-Jawzī, from Ibn ʿAbbās and others; Ibn Isḥāq gives the story at length. Al-Qurṭubī: “the commentators hold that he is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah.”

aim: The command to rise and call to Allah — and a threat to those who deny the call.
themes: The commission of the Prophet ﷺ
The prayer and feeding the poor

outline.title: The commission
outline.summary: O you enveloped in your cloak: arise and warn. Magnify your Lord. Purify your garments. Shun defilement. Do not give in order to receive more. And for your Lord’s sake, be patient.

outline.title: A hard Day
outline.summary: When the Horn is sounded, that will be a difficult Day — for the disbelievers, not easy.

outline.title: The one who thought it over
outline.summary: Leave Me with the one I created alone, and gave ample wealth, and sons at his side, and smoothed everything for; and still he wants more. He thought and plotted — may he perish, how he plotted — then looked, frowned, turned away in pride and said: “This is only magic passed on; only the word of a mortal.” I will burn him in Saqar, which spares nothing and leaves nothing. Over it are nineteen: angels, whose number We have made a test.

outline.title: One of the greatest
outline.summary: No — by the moon, and the night as it retreats, and the dawn as it brightens: it is one of the greatest of things, a warning to humankind, to whoever among you wills to go forward or to hang back.

outline.title: “What brought you to Saqar?”
outline.summary: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the people of the right hand, in gardens, asking the guilty: what led you into Saqar? They will say: we were not among those who prayed; we did not feed the poor; we waded in with those who waded in; and we denied the Day of Recompense, until the certain end came to us. No intercession will benefit them.

outline.title: Fleeing the reminder
outline.summary: What is the matter with them, turning from the reminder like startled donkeys fleeing a lion? Each of them wants to be handed scriptures unrolled. No — they do not fear the Hereafter. It is a reminder; let whoever wills remember it. He is worthy to be feared, and worthy to forgive.

keyAyah.why: Two words in Arabic — qum fa-andhir — and the beginning of twenty-three years.

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ, speaking of the pause in revelation: “While I was walking I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Ḥirāʾ, seated on a throne between the sky and the earth. I was awed by him, and went back and said: cover me, cover me. Then Allah sent down: ‘O you enveloped in your cloak, arise and warn’ — to ‘and shun defilement’. Then the revelation grew strong and came in succession.”

before: Al-Muzzammil told him to stand by night before his Lord. Al-Muddaththir tells him to stand before the people.
after: This surah ends on those who do not fear the Hereafter. Al-Qiyāmah opens by swearing by its Day.

notable.label: Every soul is held in pledge

sources: Ibn Isḥāq’s account, as the commentators relay it
